summary: The drifting cloud shade darkens soldiers, vehicles, buildings, trees and grass along with the ground.
stage: game capture: --scenario=town --seed=3 --mood=day --preset=high --perf=0 --nohud, Forward+, --fixed-fps 30, with a tank added to the scenario parked at (7, 0, 0) (scratch-only staging); the same build with --set=cloud_shadows:false (as before: shade on the ground, grass and bushes) and :true. Still: --focus=-4,-8 --zoom=26 --pitch=-45 --shot-at=40 at 1600x900. Clip: --focus=-4,-10 --zoom=28 --pitch=-45 --shot-at=27 --shots=165 --shot-every=0.1333 at 1280x720, stacked at 960x540, 15 fps (twice real speed), VP9 WebM.
rationale: The change is a moving shade, so a clip of a cloud's shade crossing a parked tank and a hamlet shows them going into it and out of it; the shade takes about 16 s to cross, so the clip runs at twice real speed, labelled. A matched still with native-resolution crops carries the comparison when paused. Both halves come from one build and one moment, with the new setting off (exactly the look before it) and on, so the clouds match frame for frame.
